It has been green\n3\ton every commit for months.\n4\t\n5\tWe shipped, and a user drained the vault with a sequence of ordinary deposit and\n6\twithdraw calls — no flash loan, no exotic cheat, nothing our invariant doesn't\n7\tcover. The drain does violate the invariant: we replayed the user's transactions\n8\tagainst the assertion by hand and it fires.\n9\t\n10\tHere is the whole test:\n11\t\n12\t    contract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n13\t        MyVault vault;\n14\t        MockERC20 token;\n15\t\n16\t        function setUp() public {\n17\t            token = new MockERC20();\n18\t            vault = new MyVault(token);\n19\t            targetContract(address(vault));\n20\t        }\n21\t\n22\t        function invariant_SolvencyHolds() public view {\n23\t            assertGe(token.balanceOf(address(vault)), vault.totalDeposits());\n24\t        }\n25\t    }\n26\t\n27\tThe assertion itself is right — it is the property we want and the drain breaks it.\n28\tSo explain what those 25,600 calls were actually doing, why none of them ever put the\n29\tvault in a state where the assertion could fail, and what we should have been looking\n30\tat in the run output that would have told us this months ago. It has been green\non every commit for months.\n\nWe shipped, and a user drained the vault with a sequence of ordinary deposit and\nwithdraw calls — no flash loan, no exotic cheat, nothing our invariant doesn't\ncover. The drain does violate the invariant: we replayed the user's transactions\nagainst the assertion by hand and it fires.\n\nHere is the whole test:\n\n    contract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n        MyVault vault;\n        MockERC20 token;\n\n        function setUp() public {\n            token = new MockERC20();\n            vault = new MyVault(token);\n            targetContract(address(vault));\n        }\n\n        function invariant_SolvencyHolds() public view {\n            assertGe(token.balanceOf(address(vault)), vault.totalDeposits());\n        }\n    }\n\nThe assertion itself is right — it is the property we want and the drain breaks it.\nSo explain what those 25,600 calls were actually doing, why none of them ever put the\nvault in a state where the assertion could fail, and what we should have been looking\nat in the run output that would have told us this months ago. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSBramJyzzu9U6Pg8L7B","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":654,"cache_read_input_tokens":22403,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":654},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4246d47f-3f7d-47b2-af59-07a04a01fc58","uuid":"d9b1efad-df3c-41b5-b3ea-df66e7937de6","timestamp":"2026-07-27T07:44:43.385Z","request_id":"req_011CdSBrZgL6hr3iQcSG8wqW"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSBramJyzzu9U6Pg8L7B","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HKeCGsPo7BU8zDV5RiyrtY","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-001/2026-07-27T074332Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why 25,600 calls never found the drain\n\n## Short version\n\nThe assertion is fine. The suite is fine. What was broken is that essentially\n**every one of those 25,600 calls reverted**, so the vault never left its initial\nstate. For months the invariant was evaluating\n\n```\nassertGe(0, 0)\n```\n\n25,600 times per run and reporting green. The suite was never capable of failing.\nThe drain sequence was not \"missed\" — no sequence could have been found, because\nthe fuzzer never got a single state-changing call through.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What the 25,600 calls were actually doing\n\n`targetContract(address(vault))` tells the invariant fuzzer: pick a random\nexternal function on `MyVault`, fill its arguments with random bytes, and call it\nfrom a random `msg.sender` drawn from the fuzzer's address pool. Repeat `depth`\ntimes, then reset state and start the next `run`.\n\nNow walk the two functions that matter with the state `setUp()` actually left\nbehind:\n\n```solidity\ntoken = new MockERC20();   // total supply 0 — nothing is ever minted\nvault  = new MyVault(token);\ntargetContract(address(vault));\n```\n\n**`deposit(uint256 amount)`**\n\n- `msg.sender` is a random address the fuzzer invented. It holds `0` tokens.\n- It has never called `token.approve(address(vault), ...)`, so its allowance is `0`.\n- `amount` is a uniform-ish draw over `uint256`, so it is astronomically large\n  almost every time (~1e77 typical).\n- The first thing `deposit` does is `token.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)`.\n  That reverts on allowance, and would revert on balance even if allowance were\n  infinite.\n\nEvery `deposit` reverts. Not most — every one.\n\n**`withdraw(uint256 amount)`**\n\n- Random sender, zero shares/zero recorded deposit.\n- Random `uint256` amount.\n- Reverts on the balance/underflow check.\n\nEvery `withdraw` reverts.\n\n**Why reverts are invisible.** The `[invariant]` section defaults to\n`fail_on_revert = false`. A reverted call is not a failure; the fuzzer discards\nit, rolls the state back, and draws the next call. A run in which 100% of calls\nrevert produces *byte-for-byte the same `[PASS]` line shape* as a run in which\n0% revert. Nothing about the green output distinguishes \"the property held under\nheavy exercise\" from \"nothing happened 25,600 times.\"\n\n**The consequence for the assertion.** With every call reverted, after each call\nthe state is still the post-`setUp()` state:\n\n- `token.balanceOf(address(vault)) == 0`\n- `vault.totalDeposits() == 0`\n\nSo the invariant checked `assertGe(0, 0)` — true, trivially, forever. There is no\nsequence of *rejected* calls that can reach a state where the assertion could\nfail, because rejected calls do not change state at all. The reachable state\nspace explored by this suite has exactly one element.\n\n**The extra irony.** `targetContract(address(vault))` *narrowed* the target set.\nWithout that line, Foundry auto-targets every contract deployed in `setUp()`,\nwhich would have included `MockERC20` and its public `mint`/`approve`. The fuzzer\nwould then have had a (very slim) chance of minting to an address and approving\nfrom that same address before depositing from it. Pinning the target to the vault\nalone removed even that accident.\n\n---\n\n## 2. What in the run output would have told you this months ago\n\n### 2a. The `reverts:` counter — it was on screen every single run\n\nFoundry prints, for every invariant test:\n\n```\n[PASS] invariant_SolvencyHolds() (runs: 512, calls: 25600, reverts: 25600)\n```\n\n`reverts: 25600` out of `calls: 25600` is the whole bug, printed on every commit\nfor months. **`reverts` approaching `calls` means the suite is testing nothing.**\nThis is the single number to read on an invariant suite, and it should be a\nreviewed metric, not incidental output. A healthy handler-driven suite sits at or\nnear `reverts: 0`.\n\nRule of thumb: anything above ~10–20% deserves investigation; anything above 50%\nmeans most of your compute is being spent generating rejected calls.\n\n### 2b. The per-selector metrics table\n\nSet (or confirm) in `foundry.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[invariant]\nshow_metrics = true\n```\n\nThis prints a per-target-function breakdown of calls / reverts / discards. It\nwould have shown `deposit` and `withdraw` at 100% reverts individually, so you\ncould not have written the aggregate number off as \"one noisy helper function.\"\n\n### 2c. `forge coverage`\n\nRun coverage over the invariant suite alone. `MyVault.deposit` and\n`MyVault.withdraw` would show their bodies at ~0% line coverage — only the\nreverting guard reached. A \"comprehensive invariant suite\" whose target contract\nshows 0% coverage on its two main functions is a contradiction that coverage\nsurfaces immediately.\n\n### 2d. A call-summary invariant (the habit that prevents this class of bug)\n\nAdd a no-op invariant whose only job is to print what the fuzzer did. Handler\nfunctions increment counters; the summary invariant logs them. Visible under\n`forge test -vv`:\n\n```\ndeposit:  8412\nwithdraw: 8390\ndonate:   8798\n```\n\nIf any line reads `0`, or the totals do not add up to `runs * depth`, the suite\nis not exercising what you think it is. This is the cheapest permanent guard\nagainst silent-no-op fuzzing.\n\n### 2e. The deepest signal: it never went red\n\nAn invariant suite that has *never* failed has never been demonstrated to be\n*able* to fail. **Negative control is mandatory.** Deliberately break the vault\n(comment out the balance decrement in `withdraw`, or bump `totalDeposits` by one\nextra wei on deposit), run the suite, and confirm it goes red and prints a\ncounterexample sequence. If it stays green, the suite proves nothing about the\ncorrect code either. Doing this once, months ago, would have caught this in\nminutes — it would have stayed green with an obviously insolvent vault.\n\nKeep this as a routine: any time you add an invariant, mutate the code to violate\nit and watch it fail before you trust it passing.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The change that makes this suite capable of finding the sequence\n\nThe fix is a **handler**: an intermediary contract that the fuzzer targets\ninstead of the vault. The handler owns the actor set, funds and approves them,\nbounds the fuzzed arguments into the legal range, and tracks ghost state. The\nfuzzer keeps its freedom over *which* action, *which* actor and *what magnitude* —\nit loses only its freedom to generate calls that are guaranteed to revert.\n\n### `test/handlers/VaultHandler.sol`\n\n```solidity\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Test, console} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {MyVault} from \"../../src/MyVault.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20} from \"../mocks/MockERC20.sol\";\n\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    MyVault  public immutable vault;\n    MockERC20 public immutable token;\n\n    uint256 constant ACTOR_COUNT   = 5;\n    uint256 constant STARTING_BAL  = 1_000_000e18;\n\n    address[] public actors;\n    address   internal currentActor;\n\n    // ---- ghost state: an independent model of what the vault should hold ----\n    uint256 public ghost_depositSum;\n    uint256 public ghost_withdrawSum;\n    uint256 public ghost_donatedSum;\n\n    mapping(bytes32 => uint256) public calls;\n\n    modifier useActor(uint256 actorSeed) {\n        currentActor = actors[bound(actorSeed, 0, actors.length - 1)];\n        vm.startPrank(currentActor);\n        _;\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    modifier countCall(bytes32 key) {\n        calls[key]++;\n        _;\n    }\n\n    constructor(MyVault _vault, MockERC20 _token) {\n        vault = _vault;\n        token = _token;\n\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < ACTOR_COUNT; i++) {\n            address actor = makeAddr(string.concat(\"actor\", vm.toString(i)));\n            actors.push(actor);\n\n            token.mint(actor, STARTING_BAL);      // <-- the funding that was missing\n            vm.prank(actor);\n            token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);  // <-- the approval that was missing\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ actions\n\n    function deposit(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 amount)\n        external\n        useActor(actorSeed)\n        countCall(\"deposit\")\n    {\n        amount = bound(amount, 0, token.balanceOf(currentActor));   // <-- the bounding that was missing\n        vault.deposit(amount);\n        ghost_depositSum += amount;\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 amount)\n        external\n        useActor(actorSeed)\n        countCall(\"withdraw\")\n    {\n        amount = bound(amount, 0, vault.maxWithdraw(currentActor)); // adapt to your accessor\n        vault.withdraw(amount);\n        ghost_withdrawSum += amount;\n    }\n\n    /// Direct token transfer to the vault, bypassing deposit accounting.\n    /// Models donation / first-depositor / share-inflation paths.\n    function donate(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 amount)\n        external\n        useActor(actorSeed)\n        countCall(\"donate\")\n    {\n        amount = bound(amount, 0, token.balanceOf(currentActor));\n        token.transfer(address(vault), amount);\n        ghost_donatedSum += amount;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers\n\n    function actorsLength() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return actors.length;\n    }\n\n    function callSummary() external view {\n        console.log(\"deposit :\", calls[\"deposit\"]);\n        console.log(\"withdraw:\", calls[\"withdraw\"]);\n        console.log(\"donate  :\", calls[\"donate\"]);\n    }\n}\n```\n\nTwo things to note about `bound`: it *reshapes* a bad draw into a legal one, so\nthe call still executes. `vm.assume` would instead *discard* the run and waste\nthe sequence — which is how suites quietly starve themselves. Use `bound` in\nhandlers, never `vm.assume`.\n\n### `test/VaultInvariant.t.sol`\n\n```solidity\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {MyVault} from \"../src/MyVault.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20} from \"./mocks/MockERC20.sol\";\nimport {VaultHandler} from \"./handlers/VaultHandler.sol\";\n\ncontract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n    MyVault      vault;\n    MockERC20    token;\n    VaultHandler handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token   = new MockERC20();\n        vault   = new MyVault(token);\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, token);\n\n        // Target the handler, not the vault.\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n\n        // Restrict to the action functions so inherited/forge-std machinery\n        // is never fuzzed.\n        bytes4[] memory selectors = new bytes4[](3);\n        selectors[0] = VaultHandler.deposit.selector;\n        selectors[1] = VaultHandler.withdraw.selector;\n        selectors[2] = VaultHandler.donate.selector;\n        targetSelector(FuzzSelector({addr: address(handler), selectors: selectors}));\n    }\n\n    // The property you already had — unchanged, and now actually reachable.\n    function invariant_SolvencyHolds() public view {\n        assertGe(token.balanceOf(address(vault)), vault.totalDeposits());\n    }\n\n    // Tighter properties that fire on the *first wei* of drift, long before\n    // the vault is actually drained.\n    function invariant_AccountingMatchesGhost() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.totalDeposits(), handler.ghost_depositSum() - handler.ghost_withdrawSum());\n    }\n\n    function invariant_SumOfSharesEqualsTotal() public view {\n        uint256 sum;\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < handler.actorsLength(); i++) {\n            sum += vault.balanceOf(handler.actors(i));\n        }\n        assertEq(sum, vault.totalSupply());\n    }\n\n    // Not an assertion — a visibility guard. Run with -vv.\n    function invariant_CallSummary() public view {\n        handler.callSummary();\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### `foundry.toml`\n\n```toml\n[invariant]\nruns           = 512\ndepth          = 100    # was 50\nfail_on_revert = true   # was implicitly false — this is the load-bearing change\nshow_metrics   = true\n```\n\n`fail_on_revert = true` is what makes the failure mode you just lived through\nimpossible to repeat. Under it, the exact bug you shipped with turns the suite\nred on the very first `deposit` call instead of hiding behind 25,600 silent\nrejections. It does impose a discipline: the handler must bound every argument so\nthat no *legitimate* call reverts. Where a revert is genuinely expected and\nacceptable, wrap that specific call in `try/catch` inside the handler and assert\non the revert reason — do not turn the flag back off to make it quiet.\n\n`depth = 50` was also too shallow. Path-dependent accounting bugs need a\ndeposit → withdraw → deposit interleaving across several actors to surface. State\nresets between runs, so depth is the only knob controlling how deep any single\nhistory goes. If wall-clock matters, trade runs for depth (`runs = 256,\ndepth = 200`) — for this bug class, depth buys more than breadth.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Confirm the new suite actually works\n\nDo not accept a green run as evidence. In order:\n\n1. `forge test --mt invariant_ -vv` — read the `reverts:` counter. It should be\n   at or near `0`, and the call summary should show all three actions with\n   healthy, roughly balanced counts.\n2. `forge coverage` — `MyVault.deposit` / `withdraw` bodies should now be\n   well covered.\n3. **Mutate the vault to reintroduce the shipped bug and rerun.** It must go red\n   and print the counterexample call sequence. Only after you have watched it\n   fail does its passing mean anything.\n4. Then revert the mutation and add a regression: assert the user's actual drain\n   sequence directly in a plain unit test, so it is pinned independently of\n   whether the fuzzer happens to rediscover it.\n\n---\n\n## Takeaway\n\n`targetContract(address(vault))` on a stateful contract with token\nprerequisites is a null test. The three things the fuzzer could not invent for\nitself — **funded actors, approvals, and in-range amounts** — are exactly what a\nhandler exists to supply. And `reverts:` in the run output is the one number that\ntells you whether an invariant suite is doing work or just spinning; it should be\nread on every run and enforced by `fail_on_revert = true`.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":654,"cache_read_input_tokens":22403,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":654},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4246d47f-3f7d-47b2-af59-07a04a01fc58","uuid":"c69e436a-b778-4373-b4b9-da8305ff5aa8","timestamp":"2026-07-27T07:45:48.019Z","request_id":"req_011CdSBrZgL6hr3iQcSG8wqW"}

The suite is fine. What was broken is that essentially\n**every one of those 25,600 calls reverted**, so the vault never left its initial\nstate. For months the invariant was evaluating\n\n```\nassertGe(0, 0)\n```\n\n25,600 times per run and reporting green. The suite was never capable of failing.\nThe drain sequence was not \"missed\" — no sequence could have been found, because\nthe fuzzer never got a single state-changing call through.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What the 25,600 calls were actually doing\n\n`targetContract(address(vault))` tells the invariant fuzzer: pick a random\nexternal function on `MyVault`, fill its arguments with random bytes, and call it\nfrom a random `msg.sender` drawn from the fuzzer's address pool. Repeat `depth`\ntimes, then reset state and start the next `run`.\n\nNow walk the two functions that matter with the state `setUp()` actually left\nbehind:\n\n```solidity\ntoken = new MockERC20();   // total supply 0 — nothing is ever minted\nvault  = new MyVault(token);\ntargetContract(address(vault));\n```\n\n**`deposit(uint256 amount)`**\n\n- `msg.sender` is a random address the fuzzer invented. It holds `0` tokens.\n- It has never called `token.approve(address(vault), ...)`, so its allowance is `0`.\n- `amount` is a uniform-ish draw over `uint256`, so it is astronomically large\n  almost every time (~1e77 typical).\n- The first thing `deposit` does is `token.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)`.\n  That reverts on allowance, and would revert on balance even if allowance were\n  infinite.\n\nEvery `deposit` reverts. Not most — every one.\n\n**`withdraw(uint256 amount)`**\n\n- Random sender, zero shares/zero recorded deposit.\n- Random `uint256` amount.\n- Reverts on the balance/underflow check.\n\nEvery `withdraw` reverts.\n\n**Why reverts are invisible.** The `[invariant]` section defaults to\n`fail_on_revert = false`. A reverted call is not a failure; the fuzzer discards\nit, rolls the state back, and draws the next call. A run in which 100% of calls\nrevert produces *byte-for-byte the same `[PASS]` line shape* as a run in which\n0% revert.
